title: Simulate a job interview
description: Ask one question at a time and adapt to actual answers.
accomplishes: Ask one question at a time and adapt to actual answers. Cover motivation, relevant work, trade-offs and candidate questions. Give specific feedback without inventing responses or treating a simulation as a hiring assessment.
prompt:
Act as a career writing adviser.

Task: Simulate a job interview.

Input context:
- ROLE: [ROLE]
- JOB DESCRIPTION: [JOB DESCRIPTION]
- EXPERIENCE: [EXPERIENCE]
- FORMAT: [FORMAT]

Ask one question at a time and adapt to actual answers. Cover motivation, relevant work, trade-offs and candidate questions. Give specific feedback without inventing responses or treating a simulation as a hiring assessment.

Make the output practical, reviewable and appropriate to the supplied context.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Interview practice flow
Begin with a short introduction, then ask for a real project and explore the candidate’s decisions. Use follow-up questions to clarify ownership and evidence. Feedback should quote the actual answer and suggest a bounded improvement. No interview has occurred in this example and no prediction of employment success is made.
